name: mcpyard
description: Small self-hosted MCP hub: one endpoint, every MCP server behind it, one key per client.

paragraphs: A small, self-hosted MCP hub. One endpoint, every MCP server behind it, one key per client.

The name comes from a switchyard, where trains are sorted onto the right track and only cleared ones get through. That is the whole job here. Clients (Claude Code, llooma, any MCP-capable agent) connect to a single /mcp endpoint; mcpyard starts and keeps the upstream MCP servers running, merges their tools, and only lets each client reach what its key allows.
Status: early, everything below works; expect rough edges before 1.0. Documentation: cedhuf.github.io/mcpyard
features: One merged endpoint. /mcp serves the tools of every server the key may see.
Known versions, one-click updates. Each server runs a package version installed by the hub,
Keys with scopes from day one. One bearer key per client, each limited to a set of servers
OIDC first. The web UI sits behind your identity provider (PocketID, Authelia, Keycloak...).
Configured by environment and one file. Runtime settings in env vars, servers in a single
